messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: [AUTO-PAGE] Elevated 5xx + timeouts detected in us-east-1 gateway cluster. 5m window: 5xx rate 13% (baseline 0.3%). Paging oncall.
carol: seeing a lot of 504s and gateway 5xx spikes on /v1/generate. Customers hitting chat endpoints.
dave: confirmed. Errors originated after a surge at ~12:10 UTC. Also CPU on scheduler pods spiked, batching queue length grew.
oncall-eng: I'm on it. pinging @runtime-sre and @gateway-team for routing and scheduler health.
runtime-sre: pulling autoscaler + batcher metrics. Queue depth on scheduler-pool-1 jumped to 12k inflight; top of queue latency > 2s -> HOL timeouts.
ml-serving: kv-cache pressure also high, lots of cache misses causing longer token-latency on hot models. Might be contributing to HOL blocking.
gateway-team: ingress shows burst from a handful of noisy customers — spike pattern: many short requests but high concurrency. Gateways queued and started returning 502/504.
product-sre: customer-impact: ~40k failed requests in last 5m, several enterprise tenants reporting errors. Working on a public note.
carol: logs snippet:
```
2026-03-15T12:11:02Z gateway ERROR upstream timeout: GET /v1/generate status=504 upstream=runtime-scheduler host=srv-1
2026-03-15T12:11:07Z scheduler WARN queue_length=12183 head_latency_ms=2345 batcher_wait_ms=340
```
dave: rolling a short snapshot of scheduler pods; trying to increase `batcher.max_concurrency` and reduce `batcher.max_batch_size` to lower HOL risk.
oncall-eng: before we do config churn, can we open fallback routing to dedicated pool? `route-policy: fallback=true` for critical customers?
runtime-sre: we can flip fallback routing to dedicated-reserve-1. Doing it now for route-tag=prod-critical. Command: `infractl route apply --from=us-east-1 --to=dedicated-reserve-1 --selector route-tag=prod-critical`
gateway-team: applied. Confirmed 3 enterprise tenants shifted to dedicated pool. Their error rates dropped to <1% within 30s.
ml-serving: also enabling local kv-cache eviction to free memory: `svcctl set kvcache.policy=lru --target=scheduler-pool-1`
carol: started a controlled restart of 2 scheduler pods to flush stuck batches (graceful drain).
dave: changed batcher config: `max_batch_size: 8 -> 4`, `batch_timeout_ms: 20 -> 10`, `concurrency_per_gpu: 4 -> 6` — aiming to reduce head-of-line wait and increase parallelism.
runtime-sre: monitoring CPU/GPU and queue depth. initial signal: queue depth down from 12k -> 3.2k in 2 minutes. 5xx rate trending down to 4%.
oncall-eng: any risk to throughput from smaller batches?
dave: throughput dip expected but latency improves; tradeoff acceptable for now. If throughput degrades we can open burst capacity.
product-sre: draft public update: "We are investigating elevated gateway errors in us-east-1; mitigation in progress, some tenants temporarily routed to dedicated capacity." Will post once we confirm stabilization.
carol: noticed a subset of long-poll requests (watch endpoints) holding runner slots and blocking tokenization. Kicking them via `kubectl delete --selector=longpoll=true` on a troubled node.
ml-serving: KV-cache eviction freed ~12GB and cache hit rate improved from 62% -> 88% on hot models. That reduced token generation tail latency.
runtime-sre: 5xx now 1.1% across cluster, timeouts down. Still seeing occasional head-of-line artifacts on one AZ: us-east-1b.
oncall-eng: handing off to @runtime-sre for monitoring and follow-up. I'm going to brief SRE rotation and customers.
product-sre: @oncall-eng can you collect impacted tenants + SLA exposure? We need to start outreach to accounts with errors > 5% during window.
oncall-eng: noted. I'll export requests by tenant between 12:05-12:20 UTC and flag >5% error.
carol: creating incident doc in ops board: https://redwood/ops/incidents/3311117777 — I've attached timeline, commands run, and heuristics.
dave: postmortem items I see immediately: 1) batcher defaults tuned for latency/throughput tradeoffs that don't handle high-concurrency short-request bursts; 2) lack of per-tenant ingress shaping; 3) insufficient kv-cache pressure alarms.
runtime-sre: follow-ups: add HOL-aware metrics (head_latency_pctiles), implement per-tenant concurrency caps, and refine autoscale triggers to consider queue length, not just CPU.
ml-serving: we'll add an adaptive kv-cache eviction policy and a low-overhead hot-model prewarm to reduce tail latency.
product-sre: outreach: initial list of 7 tenants with >10% error, 3 of them enterprise — we'll email account teams and post status.
oncall-eng: handing final actions to next shift @runtime-sre, please keep pager. Closing live paging.
runtime-sre: ack, will monitor for 60m and escalate if rates spike again.
incident-bot: Incident resolved: 5xx rates returned to baseline. Pages closed. Summary: routing fallback + batcher config change + kv-cache eviction restored service.
carol: quick notes for postmortem: timeline, commands, root causes, mitigation runbook updates. I'll assign owners.
dave: thanks team. We'll schedule a retro and update playbooks: add a "bursty short-request" mode, and test fallback routing automation. :thumbsup:
product-sre: I'll own customer comms and post-incident report.
runtime-sre: last check at 12:40 UTC: queue depth steady ~150, 5xx <0.2%. Leaving monitoring on.
carol: closing thread, will link postmortem when ready.
